question: Does the trained-loop depth/gate/bank behavior reproduce at small scale with the reference implementation?

data.name: WikiText-103 raw
data.tokenizer: 16k byte-level BPE trained on a 50M-char sample

control_82m.note: Same token checkpoint for both models. The 1-pass control is flat across inference passes; the 3-pass model is much worse when its trained passes are removed.

control_90m_note.note: The 1-pass run reached 90M tokens before a display-GPU hang stopped it; the depth curve was already flat. The 82M checkpoint is the reproducible comparison.

findings: The 3-pass-trained model is best at 3 passes at 120M tokens: 36.61 PPL vs 40.75 at 2 (+11.3%), 37.42 at 4 (+2.2%), and 52.81 at 1 (+44.3%).
The 1-pass control is flat across 1/2/3/4 passes at 82M (41.41/41.45/41.44/41.45) and at 90M (40.33/40.32/40.35/40.32). Extra inference passes do not help a model trained without the loop.
The 3-pass model is much worse at 1 pass (56.38 at 82M; 52.81 at 120M), showing that the trained schedule is part of the function, not an optional inference setting.

The block-bank read is the dominant component at small scale: zeroing the read queries gives 381.05 PPL (+879%). The per-layer message gates cost +44.9%; the shared message-read query alone costs +1.6%.
The 4-pass penalty is much smaller than at 26B (+2.2% here vs +52% there). The depth preference is real but scale/training dependent; the 35B pilot must measure it rather than assume the 26B gap.
This reproduces the 26B qualitative story at 23M: the loop is a trained prior; the bank and message channel are load-bearing; the architecture is portable but the weights are not.
caveats: 16k BPE and a 128-token sliding window are scaled ratios, not the 26B model's exact tokenizer/window.
The 1-pass control was stopped at 90M tokens by a display-GPU hang; the 82M checkpoint is the reproducible same-token comparison.
The ablation baseline (38.92, 8 eval batches) and the depth table (36.61, 4 eval batches) use different validation subsets.
This is a mechanism reproduction, not a capability or long-context claim.

artifacts.data: WikiText-103 raw; token arrays are generated by scripts/prepare_wikitext.py
